chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Regarding a man who prays salat facing other than the qibla and realizes this while in the salat, before he has completed it — he said: If he was facing somewhere between the east and the west, let him turn his face toward the qibla the moment he realizes it; and if he was facing the back of the qibla (directly opposite), let him cut short the salat, then turn his face toward the qibla, then begin the salat anew.

key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: Qibla — the direction of prayer toward the Ka'ba in Mecca, obligatory for valid salat
key_terms.دُبُرِ الْقِبْلَةِ: Dubur al-qibla — the back/opposite of the qibla, meaning facing entirely away from Mecca
key_terms.يَفْتَتِحُ الصَّلَاةَ: To begin/open the salat anew — the technical expression for commencing salat from the start

ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if they realize during prayer that they are not facing the qibla?
ai.summary: Imam Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the legal ruling for a person who realizes mid-prayer that they are not facing the qibla. The ruling differentiates between two degrees of error: facing somewhere in the general east-west arc (a minor deviation) requires immediate correction without restarting, while facing the complete opposite direction (dubur al-qibla) requires breaking and restarting the prayer entirely. This hadith was narrated through Ammar al-Sabati, a prolific Fathi narrator of Imam Sadiq's legal rulings, and reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of proportionality in correcting ritual errors.
